PARAM_SCALES.doc: How a host draws a parameter: linear, logarithmic (a frequency, a time) or in discrete steps. The words omx-plugins' declarations and plugin-hostd's protocol use; a travel names its own with `scale`.

READOUT_RATE_HZ.doc: How often a readout's value is published: 50 Hz, one value every 20 ms, the rate a host sends a moving meter at. Every readout reads it as its `rateHz` (docs/readouts.md).

STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES.doc: The standard sample rates (Hz) the desk recognises — the pro-audio superset. One source of truth for the clock controller's `clock.allowed-rates` seed, the force row's validation ceiling and the device-rate probe fallback. What the operator is OFFERED is always the DEVICE's own `supportedRates` — this is the ceiling a write is refused by, never a menu.

ORACLE_FLOOR_RATES.doc: The four rates every kernel oracle runs at, whatever STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES says: a declared list missing one of them stops a suite instead of testing less (omx-dsp, omx-plugins and omx-clap-host run their oracles at these).

ORACLE_FULL_RATES.doc: The full grid of rates a professional interface can clock at, nine of them from 32 to 192 kHz: where ORACLE_FLOOR_RATES is the four rates every kernel oracle must run at, this is the whole grid an oracle runs at when it runs at all of them. STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES is a subset of it; an oracle that runs here also covers 32, 64 and 128 kHz, where a kernel still has to meet its closed form even though the console never asks for them.
